title: Activation coupling map + resilience slate
body:
Purpose:
This working slate stitches together a lightweight roadmap tracker, a compact KPI sheet, and a launch readiness checklist focused on coupling risk and operational resilience. Intended to be a single-pane briefing for the cross-functional launch lead and on-call rotations during ramp.

Audience:
- Product Ops (primary)
- Eng (serving-runtime, infra, hosted-api)
- SRE & Observability
- Solutions & Customer Success

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Target launch window: week of 2026-04-06 (soft beta) -> 2026-05-04 (wide roll)
- Critical path: model-variant pinning -> runtime kernel selection QA -> canary capacity policy -> telemetry gating
- Acceptance guard: 99th pct latency < 850ms on canary, error rate < 0.8% sustained for 48h, adoption signal SLO (first-1000 users) above 60% success rate

1) Roadmap tracker (one-line cadence + owners)
- Novice-to-stable ramp lanes: alpha (teams internal) / beta (select customers) / general availability
- Sprint cadence: 2-week sprint alignment; launch-focused milestones anchored to sprints 2026-03 (stabilize), 2026-04 (beta), 2026-05 (scale)
- Milestones (owner)
  - M1: Model variant QA complete (Rohit Verma)
  - M2: Runtime perf regressions < 5% vs baseline (Claire Zhang)
  - M3: Canary policy + autoscale templates in Prod (Noah Patel)
  - M4: Observability dashboards + alert playbooks (Maya Thompson)

2) Compact KPI sheet (baseline + target + gating thresholds)
- KPI: 99th pct token-latency (baseline: 720ms) -> beta target: < 850ms -> GA target: < 700ms
- KPI: Token cost per 1k (baseline: $2.40) -> target reduce by 20% by GA
- KPI: Request error rate (baseline: 0.6%) -> canary gate: < 0.8% sustained 48h
- KPI: Model-quality regression (eval prompt-set) -> pass rate >= 95% on shadow A/B
- KPI: Availability per region -> 99.9% during business hours on Dedicated customers
- Tracking cadence: metrics snapshot daily during beta, hourly during 24h of scale tests

3) Coupling & dependency map (critical vs nice-to-have)
- Critical dependencies (high coupling):
  - Model artifact pinning (model ops) -> if delayed, roll must use fallback model variants; owner: Rohit
  - Kernel/quantization parity on dedicated GPUs -> owner: Claire (perf eng)
  - Autoscaling + burst policy templates (infra) -> owner: Noah
  - Observability hook + trace propagation (obs) -> owner: Maya
- Medium coupling:
  - Console rollout controls (product) -> nice but can be toggled off
  - Billing metering tags (finance) -> affects cost reporting, not launch gate
- Dependency notes: anything that sits in the critical list has explicit rollback and fallback documented in the incident-sim section below.

4) Readiness checklist (go/no-go rows) - one-line status + owner
- Model QA completed: IN_PROGRESS (Rohit)
- Runtime regression < 5%: PASS (Claire)
- Canary autoscale policy validated in staging: IN_PROGRESS (Noah)
- End-to-end smoke tests (ramp simulator): PENDING (SRE)
- Dashboards and alerting configured: IN_PROGRESS (Maya)
- Customer beta cohort informed and NDA confirmed: DONE (Solutions)

5) Incident simulation (3 tabletop scenarios + playbooks)
- Scenario A: Sudden 3x traffic spike -> immediate effect: queue growth, elevated latencies; playbook: trigger burst pool, shift noncritical routes to lower-tier model variant, page infra on-call, initiate customer-facing message if >15 min impact
- Scenario B: Model quality regression (regression alerts fire on eval-set) -> immediate effect: decrease in pass-rate, downstream churn risk; playbook: auto-fallback to previous model pin for live traffic, snapshot traces, open postmortem ticket, stop GA expansion until root cause triaged
- Scenario C: Region outage during ramp (AZ-level) -> immediate effect: partial capacity loss; playbook: route traffic to alternate region, enforce stricter rate limiting per-token, engage SRE-runbooks for cross-region capacity, notify customers and enable delay-tolerant degrade mode

6) Escalation matrix (who to page in order)
- P1 page: on-call SRE -> infra lead (Noah) -> runtime eng (Claire) -> product ops lead (Ethan) -> Exec escalation if >2h unresolved
- Communication channels: #launch-control Slack, PagerDuty escalation, Confluence status page (linked above)

7) SLO gates & Go/No-go criteria (explicit numeric thresholds)
- Canary open gate for GA expansion if all true:
  - 99th pct latency on canary < 850ms for 48h
  - Error rate on canary < 0.8% for 48h
  - Model eval pass-rate >= 95% on evaluation suite for 48h
  - No open P1s tied to the release (owner-confirmed)

8) Rollback / fallback templates
- Soft rollback: route 30% traffic to fallback model variant for 1 hour while monitoring KPIs
- Full rollback: revert routing to last-stable model and scale down canary; trigger RCA and stop wider roll
- After rollback checklist: capture KV cache state, preserve trace ids, archive diagnostics to S3 bucket (path in linked_artifacts)

9) Ramp schedule + staffing (ops rota)
- Beta week (04/06): 08:00-20:00 local coverage by product-ops + obs lead; overnight on-call SRE
- Scale week (05/04): full 24/7 rotation for first 72 hours; exec check-ins twice daily

10) Open questions / action items (owner, due)
- Q1: Confirm fallback model variants meet QA (Rohit, due 2026-03-14)
- A1: Validate autoscale template under synthetic 10k rps (Noah, due 2026-03-21)
- Q2: Add explicit billing tagging for surge events (Finance & Claire, due 2026-03-18)
Notes & provenance:
- This is intentionally terse — keep this file as the operational slate that aligns with the more formal activation-coupling-canvas in Confluence (see linked_artifacts). Use this doc for daily stand check-ins during ramp.

Next steps:
- Owners above to update the small KPI sheet (linked) with daily snapshots; product-ops will consolidate into the launch status email each morning during beta.
- Schedule a full tabletop with the SRE rota next Wednesday (calendar invite pending).

-- Ethan (product-ops)
